steps.text: Bring chicken, water, and chicken stock to a simmer in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Reduce the heat to medium-low and continue to simmer until chicken is no longer pink in the center, about 20 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside to cool. Reserve the cooking liquid.

While the chicken is cooling, heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and garlic; cook and stir until onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. Add potatoes, then strain the reserved cooking liquid into the pot. Increase the heat to high and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer until potatoes are tender, about 25 minutes.

Cut cooked chicken into cubes and add to simmering potatoes; cook for 5 minutes. Stir in garbanzo beans, spinach, and roasted red peppers; simmer for 10 more minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle with Parmesan before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken, Spinach, and Potato Soup
raw_recipe.description: This chicken and spinach soup is hearty and delicious. With potatoes, garbanzo beans, roasted red peppers, and Parmesan cheese, it’s a meal in a bowl!
raw_recipe.name: Chicken, Spinach, and Potato Soup

review.reviewBody: This was the greatest recipe for soup I have ever had!!! I omitted the garbanzo beans, red peppers, and parmesan cheese, which took the calories per cup down to 150 - I think it's the olive oil that makes it taste so good, and if you're using bouillion, I highly recommend "Better than Bouillion" - lower in sodium, and tastes more like real chicken broth straight from the stock pot!

This soup is AWESOME! Hubby and I were able to stop eating it ONLY after our stomachs protested that they were way too full! Very filling soup. Made a few changes: 1/2 diced onion, 1 1/2 t. salt, 1/2 t. miso. I didn't have roasted red peppers, so I used 1/2 c. diced green pepper and roasted it in a black iron skillet in 1 t. olive oil and 1/2 t. sugar (could use soy sauce instead of sugar if not using miso) till the edges were brown. Left out the Parmesan cheese and served over jasmine rice. Added pepper to taste in individual bowls. This is definitely going in our regular rotation! YUM!!

I used leftover cooked chicken and broth made from the chicken breast bones (boil 20 mins, harvest what chicken was left on the bones and the broth). The secret is you should grate the potatoes, not cut them in chunks. The soup cooks faster and gives you a nice creamy texture. I forgot to add the parmesan, added some dry parsley, a cup of frozen peas and a pkg of frozen spinach. This is a keeper!

This soup is great! I added andouille sausage and red pepper flakes, reduced the liquid to 4 cups (2 cups stock, 1 cup white wine and 1 cup water), and browned the chicken thighs in oil and lemon pepper. After browning the chicken, I took it out to cut up, then cooked the garlic and onion in the same pot, then added the potatoes, liquid and cut-up chicken back in to cook together. This sped up the overall cooking time and also let the flavors meld together better. I put in the pre-cooked sausage (which made the dish in my opinion) at the same time as the beans and spinach. With the andouille sausage and red pepper flakes, this soup was a flavorful hit on a cold night.

Very delicious soup!! I was pleasantly surprised by it!
What I did personally was that I omitted the garbanzo beans (we don't care for them) and bell peppers (did not have any this time). Instead I chopped up three large carrots and used minced garlic from a jar,and added that with the spinach and potatoes (the spinach or any similar green gives it a nice delicious, leafy crunch by the way. Definitely use veggies in a soup. :-)

Plus, you may possibly end up with not enough broth. In case you'll have to make do with what you have to make more - such as chicken stock or more water to simmer in with the chicken flavor. I also added lots of parmesan cheese, probably more than was stated in the recipe. Delicious! And I'm also adding more as I'm eating the leftovers for breakfast this morning.

Overall, this soup is DELICIOUS and I'll definitely make it again along with any other soups I want to try. You can always add a few minor alterations depending on your taste preferences. Great for a cool - weather dinner and any quick, delicious meal.
I added a roma tomato and a tsp of sundried tomato paste, and then pureed the entire thing for my baby. He Loved it. Capscicum addition was a great idea.

Excellent soup! Instead of poaching the chicken I browned it with lemon pepper seasoning in the soup pot. That added a lot of flavor to the broth. Also added some carrots, celery and leeks that I needed to use up (and let's face it, you can never go wrong putting those veggies in a soup!). Used 4 cups water and 4 cups chicken stock.

OMG this was sooo good and easy! I changed this up slightly, so that it was a one pot dish. I sauteed the onions and garlic, then pushed those to one side to brown the chicken in the same skillet. I deglazed with some red wine, since I had just opened a bottle. Then I added the potatoes and water/broth and simmered until everything was cooked through. I generally like thicker broths, while my fiance likes thinner broths, and this was a perfect compromise. Was also great because you could throw in any veggies that you have! We only had great northern beans, so I used those. I also didn't bother with the cheese because I thought it had plenty of flavor without.
Loved it! I made it in the crockpot and did not cook the chicken. At the end of 8 hours on low I added a cut up block of cream cheese, let it melt and stirred it in! :)

Disclaimer: I didn't have a few ingredients so I had to make a few modifications... but it was delicious! I left out the garbanzo beans and red peppers because I did not have them, and used leftover grilled chicken re-heated in the broth/water mixture. I added some crushed red pepper to the onions/garlic for spice, and the potatoes only took about 10 minutes to cook once I added the cooking liquid. For the last 5 minutes I added the Parmesan, Spinach, some Crumbled Bacon and some tempered Greek Yogurt for creaminess. It had great depth of flavor for such a short cook-time! This recipe is so versatile, I will definitely be making this again with whatever ingredients I have on hand ;)
Used 4 cups of low sodium broth and one cup of water. Also, added extra fresh garlic. Browned thighs first.
I can't wait to make it again. It was so delicious.
We loved it, but it needs more flavor for us. Next time, I will add bay leaves.

I considered not adding the garbanzo beans, but am glad I did. The texture was great - a pop of creaminess. I had no roasted peppers and didn’t miss them. My husband said it’s a keeper! Try it for a delicious and healthy meal.

I followed the recipe pretty much to a T. It’s a good base recipe and tastes good on its own but the flavor would be improved with something from the spice cabinet: perhaps rosemary, marjoram, or a bay leaf. I used about 10 twists each of cracked black pepper and pink Himalayan salt. Considering adding a carrot or two.
My favorite soup to make. It’s filling, low calorie, high protein and my go-to comfort food.
This is a fantastic soup. Can be added to. I added more seasoning. Got the kids to eat spinach. They didn't even realize. Will be making this often.
This is the second time I made this soup. It is so yummy. Didn’t have garbanzo beans so substituted cannellini beans. Used leftover chicken pieces. WONDERFUL!
I added 1 tsp of Worcestershire sauce and 1 Roma tomato - my husband loved it

Attractive and flavorful! I followed the recipe almost exactly except shredded the chicken instead of cubing it and left out the beans this time. Next time -- and there definitely will be a next time! -- I'll try mashing or blending some of the potatoes to thicken the broth a bit. Thanks for sharing this recipe.
